prs.title: Fix completed request cancellation cleanup
prs.author: FU-max-boop
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: RequestResponder cancellation lifecycle is broken in two interacting ways: (1) cancel() incorrectly sends an error response for cancelled requests, violating the MCP spec rule that receivers must not respond to cancelled requests; (2) when the cancel scope is cancelled and _completed is already True, _cancel_scope.__exit__ raises CancelledExc that propagates out of the context manager. Both defects live in the same 30-line cancel/exit sequence and stem from the same root cause: the cancellation cleanup path was never fully spec-compliant. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: RequestResponder cancellation lifecycle is broken in two interacting ways: (1) cancel() incorrectly sends an error response for cancelled requests, violating the MCP spec rule that receivers must not respond to cancelled requests; (2) when the cancel scope is cancelled and _completed is already True, _cancel_scope.__exit__ raises CancelledExc that propagates out of the context manager. Both defects live in the same 30-line cancel/exit sequence and stem from the same root cause: the cancellation cleanup path was never fully spec-compliant. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: PR #2624 includes test infrastructure (new imports in test_session.py) and its try/except guard — conditioned on `self._completed and isinstance(exc, CancelledExc)` — is the mechanically precise fix that subsumes the cleanup problem. PR #2493's server.py change (early return on cancellation) and its removal of the error-response send in cancel() must still be incorporated, but #2624 is the better base: it adds coverage and the exception guard handles the cleanup correctly regardless of whether #2493's server-side early-return is present.

clusters.pick_reason: PR #2624 includes test infrastructure (new imports in test_session.py) and its try/except guard — conditioned on `self._completed and isinstance(exc, CancelledExc)` — is the mechanically precise fix that subsumes the cleanup problem. PR #2493's server.py change (early return on cancellation) and its removal of the error-response send in cancel() must still be incorporated, but #2624 is the better base: it adds coverage and the exception guard handles the cleanup correctly regardless of whether #2493's server-side early-return is present.

members.title: fix: don't send a response for cancelled requests
members.author: Zelys-DFKH
members.reason: [llm] duplicates #2624: RequestResponder cancellation lifecycle is broken in two interacting ways: (1) cancel() incorrectly sends an error response for cancelled requests, violating the MCP spec rule that receivers must not respond to cancelled requests; (2) when the cancel scope is cancelled and _completed is already True, _cancel_scope.__exit__ raises CancelledExc that propagates out of the context manager. Both defects live in the same 30-line cancel/exit sequence and stem from the same root cause: the cancellation cleanup path was never fully spec-compliant.
